answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it may post bids, then weight influence by value at risk rather than by account count. If identities coordinate to fake demand or capture rewards, proof of collusion or failed delivery burns their stake, while creating many accounts multiplies the capital required. A dawn-to-nadir participation history can expose sudden Sybil swarms, but the bridge is the costly bond: attackers must put real value at risk for every identity.
